method_card.title: Jobs and Work Experience
method_card.content:
This lesson covers jobs vocabulary, work experience (las prácticas) and giving opinions about future careers. The key grammar rule is that ser + profession takes NO article in Spanish.

SpanishEnglish
médico / médicadoctor (m/f)
enfermero / enfermeranurse (m/f)
profesor / profesorateacher (m/f)
ingeniero / ingenieraengineer (m/f)
abogado / abogadalawyer (m/f)
contableaccountant
camarero / camarerawaiter / waitress
periodistajournalist (m/f same)
electricistaelectrician (m/f same)
las prácticaswork experience (always plural)
el sueldosalary / wage
el empleoemployment / job
el desempleounemployment
trabajar de / comoto work as

Grammar focus — ser + profession (NO article): In Spanish you say Soy profesor (I am a teacher) — NEVER Soy un profesor. The indefinite article (un/una) is omitted before a profession after ser unless there is an adjective modifying the noun: Soy un profesor muy exigente (I am a very demanding teacher — adjective forces the article back). Use trabajar de / trabajar como to say what you work as: Trabajo de camarero (I work as a waiter).

Model paragraph: Me gustaría ser médica porque quiero ayudar a la gente. Hice las prácticas en una oficina el año pasado y trabajé de recepcionista. Fue muy interesante aunque el sueldo era bajo.
(I would like to be a doctor because I want to help people. I did work experience in an office last year and worked as a receptionist. It was very interesting although the salary was low.)
steps: Learn jobs vocabulary with the correct gender endings (médico/médica, ingeniero/ingeniera)
Master the rule: ser + profession takes NO article — Soy profesor, not Soy un profesor
Use me gustaría ser + profession to talk about future career ambitions
Practise describing work experience using the preterite tense with hice las prácticas

exam_context.frequency: Core topic across Theme 5 — jobs and future opportunities

worked_examples.question: Translate: Quiero ser ingeniera porque me gustan las ciencias.

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Quiero ser = I want to be. Note: ser + profession — no article needed.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: ingeniera = engineer (feminine form — the speaker is female). porque me gustan las ciencias = because I like Science (gustan plural).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I want to be an engineer because I like Science.

worked_examples.question: Spot the error: 'Soy un abogado y trabajo en una oficina.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: After ser, Spanish does NOT use the article before an unmodified profession.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Soy un abogado has an unnecessary un. The correct form is Soy abogado. The article would only return if you added an adjective: Soy un abogado famoso.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The error is un — it should be removed. Correct: Soy abogado y trabajo en una oficina.

worked_examples.question: Translate into Spanish: 'Last summer I did work experience in a hospital. I worked as a nurse and it was very rewarding.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Work experience = las prácticas (always plural). I did = hice (preterite of hacer). Last summer = el verano pasado.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: I worked as = trabajé de / trabajé como (preterite). Nurse = enfermero/a. It was = fue (preterite of ser). Rewarding = gratificante.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: El verano pasado hice las prácticas en un hospital. Trabajé de enfermero y fue muy gratificante.

bronze.question: Match the Spanish jobs to their English meaning
Match the Spanish work phrases to their English meaning
Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: porque me gustan las ciencias. Mi madre es

gaps.correct_explain: médico (or another profession) — after quiero ser, use the profession with no article. Quiero ser médico, NOT quiero ser un médico.

wrong.un médico: The indefinite article is omitted after ser before an unmodified profession. Say ser médico, not ser un médico.
wrong.una médica: The indefinite article is omitted after ser before an unmodified profession. Say ser médica, not ser una médica.

gaps.correct_explain: enfermera — use the feminine form because mi madre is feminine. No article after ser.

wrong.una enfermera: No article after es before an unmodified profession. Say es enfermera.

gaps.correct_explain: hice is the yo form of hacer in the preterite. Irregular: hice, hiciste, hizo...

wrong.hacé: hacé does not exist. The yo preterite of hacer is hice.
wrong.hizo: hizo is the él/ella form. The subject is 'I' → hice.

gaps.correct_explain: Trabajé is the yo form of trabajar in the preterite: -ar verb → -é.

wrong.Trabajo: Trabajo is present tense. 'Last summer' requires the preterite → trabajé.
wrong.Trabajaba: Trabajaba is imperfect — used for habitual/ongoing past. A specific event 'last summer' uses the preterite → trabajé.

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I am a teacher'?
What does 'Me gustaría ser abogada porque me interesa la justicia' mean?
options: I would like to be a lawyer because justice interests me
I am a lawyer because justice interests me
I want to be a lawyer because I like the law
I used to be a lawyer because I liked justice

bronze.source_text: Mi padre es ingeniero y trabaja en una empresa grande. Gana un buen sueldo.
model_answers: My father is an engineer and works in a big company. He earns a good salary.

silver.question: Complete the sentence

gaps.correct_explain: me gustaría = I would like. Conditional tense, 1st person singular of gustar. More polite and future-oriented than quiero.

wrong.me gustó: me gustó is preterite (I liked — past). Use me gustaría (I would like) for future wishes.

gaps.correct_explain: me encanta or me gusta + infinitive = I love/like to + verb. The verb is singular because the 'thing liked' is an action (infinitive).

wrong.encantan: me encantan is plural. With an infinitive, use the singular → me encanta.

silver.english: When I finish school, I would like to be a journalist because I love writing.

silver.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
silver.sentence: Mi hermana es una abogada muy buena y trabaja en Madrid.
silver.explanation: After ser, the indefinite article is omitted before a profession unless an adjective modifies the noun. Es una abogada muy buena is actually acceptable here because muy buena modifies abogada — but the base rule is es abogada without the article. The error to correct is to remove the article: Mi hermana es abogada muy buena.
silver.translation: My sister is a very good lawyer and works in Madrid.

silver.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
silver.english: Last summer I did work experience in a hospital and it was very interesting.

distractor_labels.hizo: wrong person — hizo is él/ella (he/she did). The subject is yo (I) → hice

silver.source_text: My brother is a mechanic and earns a good salary. I would like to be a journalist because I love writing.
model_answers: Mi hermano es mecánico y gana un buen sueldo. Me gustaría ser periodista porque me encanta escribir.

gold.source_text: Last year I did work experience in a law firm for two weeks. I worked as a receptionist and it was very useful. In the future I would like to be a lawyer because I find the justice system fascinating.
model_answers: El año pasado hice las prácticas en un bufete de abogados durante dos semanas. Trabajé de recepcionista y fue muy útil. En el futuro me gustaría ser abogada porque encuentro el sistema de justicia fascinante.

gold.question: Build the sentence in Spanish
gold.english: In the future I would like to work as a journalist because I want to earn a good salary.

distractor_labels.trabajo: wrong form — after me gustaría, use the infinitive trabajar, not conjugated trabajo
distractor_labels.gano: wrong form — after quiero, use the infinitive ganar, not conjugated gano
distractor_labels.me gusta: wrong tense — me gusta is present (I like). The English says 'I would like' → me gustaría

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a café in Spain talking to a Spanish student about jobs and work experience.

bullets.prompt: Say what job you would like to do in the future and why.
bullets.model_answer: Me gustaría ser médico porque quiero ayudar a la gente y me gustan las ciencias.
bullets.note: me gustaría + ser + profession (no article) + porque + reason

bullets.prompt: Describe your work experience — where you went and what you did.
bullets.model_answer: El verano pasado hice las prácticas en una oficina. Trabajé de recepcionista durante dos semanas.
bullets.note: preterite: hice (hacer), trabajé (trabajar) — both completed past events; trabajé de + profession (no article)

bullets.prompt: Give your opinion on the work experience and say what you learned.
bullets.model_answer: Fue muy útil porque aprendí a usar el ordenador y a hablar por teléfono. Sin embargo, el sueldo era bajo.
bullets.note: fue (preterite of ser for opinion) + aprendí a + infinitive; sin embargo (connective)

bullets.prompt: Ask your partner what job they would like to do.
bullets.model_answer: ¿Y tú, qué te gustaría ser en el futuro?
bullets.note: ¿qué te gustaría ser? — conditional question, no article before profession

gold.question: Write 40-50 words in Spanish about your future career and any work experience you have done. Include: the job you would like to do and why, details of work experience (real or imaginary), your opinion of that experience, and one thing you learned.

Mark on: Communication (future job, work experience details, opinion, learning point — all addressed?), Range of language (me gustaría + infinitive, preterite for past events, connectives like sin embargo/también, opinion phrases), Accuracy (ser + profession — no article, preterite forms hice/trabajé/fue, adjective agreement). Be encouraging and formative. Respond in JSON: {"quality":"excellent|good|needs_work|not_valid","feedback":"3-4 sentences covering each criterion","improvement":"One specific grammar point to work on"}

gold.audio_text: El año pasado hice las prácticas en una empresa. Trabajé de recepcionista y fue muy interesante aunque el sueldo era bajo.
gold.correct_text: El año pasado hice las prácticas en una empresa. Trabajé de recepcionista y fue muy interesante aunque el sueldo era bajo.
gold.translation: Last year I did work experience in a company. I worked as a receptionist and it was very interesting although the salary was low.

gold.question: Complete the sentence
sentence_parts: la oportunidad de hacer las prácticas antes de

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive after es importante que
gaps.correct_explain: tengan is the present subjunctive of tener (ellos/ellas/ustedes). After es importante que, use the subjunctive.

wrong.tienen: tienen is the present indicative. After es importante que, Spanish requires the present subjunctive → tengan.
wrong.tener: tener is the infinitive. After es importante que + a subject, use the subjunctive → tengan.

gaps.correct_explain: elegir (to choose) — after antes de, use the infinitive.

wrong.eligen: eligen is conjugated. After antes de, use the infinitive → elegir.

gold.english: It is important that young people have the opportunity to do work experience before choosing a career.
